'''Nissan Slomiansky''' ({{langx|he|ניסן סלומיאנסקי}}; born 10 January 1946) is an Israeli politician. He served as a member of the [[Knesset]] for the [[National Religious Party]] between 1996 and 1999, and again from 2003-2009, and was re-elected again in 2013, serving until 2019. He is a member of the [[Jewish Home]] party.

==Biography==
Slomiansky was born in [[Ramat Gan]] during the [[Mandatory Palestine|Mandate era]] in the family, who migrated from the [[Second Polish Republic]]. He was educated at [[Bnei Akiva]]'s [[yeshiva]] in Nechalim, and completed academic studies in [[physics]] and [[mathematics]] at [[Bar-Ilan University]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2025}} He also studied in the Hesder [[Yeshivat Kerem B'Yavneh]], where he was certified as a teacher and ordained as a [[Rabbi]]. After his studies, he enlisted to the Nahal Paratroopers unit and reached the rank of first lieutenant.{{Citation needed|date=July 2025}} Thereafter, he turned to politics, serving for more than two decades from 1977 to 1998 as the first head of [[Elkana]] local council. He was also the secretary-general of [[Gush Emunim]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=German |first=Atara |date=2019-01-17 |title=ניסן סלומינסקי הודיע על פרישה מהחיים הפוליטיים |url=https://www.srugim.co.il/306887-%d7%a0%d7%99%d7%a1%d7%9f-%d7%a1%d7%9c%d7%95%d7%9e%d7%99%d7%a0%d7%a1%d7%a7%d7%99-%d7%94%d7%95%d7%93%d7%99%d7%a2-%d7%a2%d7%9c-%d7%a4%d7%a8%d7%99%d7%a9%d7%94-%d7%9e%d7%94%d7%97%d7%99%d7%99%d7%9d-%d7%94 |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=Srugim |language=HE}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{MKlink|id=92}}</ref>

In the [[1996 Israeli legislative election|1996 elections]], Slomiansky was placed 10th on the National Religious Party's list of candidates. He entered the Knesset in May 1997, following the death of [[Avraham Stern (politician)|Avraham Stern]]. He lost his seat in the [[1999 Israeli legislative election|1999 elections]], but regained it in [[2003 Israeli legislative election|2003]] when he was placed sixth on the party's list of candidates. He was later re-elected to the Seventeenth Knesset in [[2006 Israeli legislative election|2006]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

During the Sixteenth Knesset (2003-2006), Slomiansky headed the parliamentary lobby for elderly persons, and served as the chairperson of the party's Knesset caucus. For the [[2009 Israeli legislative election|2009 elections]], he won a fourth place on [[the Jewish Home]] list, but lost his seat when the party won only three seats. In the [[2013 Israeli legislative election|2013 election]], he was placed third on the Jewish Home list and was re-elected to Knesset.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 |url=https://en.idi.org.il/israeli-elections-and-parties/elections/2013/ |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=en.idi.org.il |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 |url=https://en.idi.org.il/israeli-elections-and-parties/elections/2009/ |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=en.idi.org.il |language=en}}</ref> In 2011, he was appointed Vice President of the [[Lander Institute]], replacing retired General [[Yaakov Amidror]], who was appointed Head of the [[National Security Council (Israel)|National Security Council]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-03-28 |title=סלומינסקי- סגן נשיא מכון לנדר |url=https://www.kipa.co.il/%D7%97%D7%93%D7%A9%D7%95%D7%AA/%d7%a1%d7%9c%d7%95%d7%9e%d7%99%d7%a0%d7%a1%d7%a7%d7%99-%d7%a1%d7%92%d7%9f-%d7%a0%d7%a9%d7%99%d7%90-%d7%9e%d7%9b%d7%95%d7%9f-%d7%9c%d7%a0%d7%93%d7%a8/ |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=כיפה |language=he-IL}}</ref>

Following allegations of sexual misconduct in December 2016,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-16 |title=Israeli Lawmaker Nissan Slomiansky Accused of Sexual Misconduct |url=https://forward.com/israel/357211/israeli-lawmaker-nissan-slomiansky-accused-of-sexual-misconduct/ |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=The Forward |language=en}}</ref> Slomiansky suspended himself from the chairmanship of the Knesset's [[Constitution, Law and Justice Committee]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pyutrikovsky |first=Shlomo |title=Tzfat rabbi delivers testimony on Slomiansky case |url=https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/223361 |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=Israel National News |language=en}}</ref> A police investigation into Slomiansky's conduct was closed in 2017 due to lack of evidence.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-03-12 |title=נסגר התיק נגד ח"כ סלומינסקי בשל חוסר ראיות מספיקות |url=https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5051350,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250714115243/https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5051350,00.html |archive-date=2025-07-14 |access-date=2025-07-18 |work=ynet |language=he |url-status=live }}</ref>

Slomiansky retired from political life in January 2019, and left the Knesset after the [[April 2019 Israeli legislative election|April 2019 election]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2019-01-17 |title=ח"כ ניסן סלומינסקי פורש מהחיים הפוליטיים |url=https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5448670,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250223235114/https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5448670,00.html |archive-date=2025-02-23 |access-date=2025-07-18 |work=ynet |language=he |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Family==
Slomiansky is married, and a father of five children.<ref>[http://baityehudi.org.il/englp/nisan.htm Profile]{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}, baityehudi.org.il; accessed 31 July 2015.</ref>
